author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: The front end is doing the Fed's work before lift-off (2Y 1.52%, +48 bps over 20 observations, a bear flattening to +51 bps) while minutes leave the March step size open and Russia's claimed pull-back eases gas and the VIX against NATO reports of a continuing build-up; the edge is short duration, energy, materials and pricing-power cyclicals plus policy divergence (China easing, Polish banks on 9.2% inflation), not long-duration growth, where pandemic-fade results (Roblox, Shopify) were punished and reopening or cash-return beats (Airbnb, Cisco, DoorDash) rewarded.
sources_policy: Only the 2022-02-17 frozen feed (via tools/digest.py and tools/cited_titles.py) and the 2022-02-17 market card (tools/showcard.py) were used; every cited ID was re-checked against its own-date headline, publication stamp (strictly before 2022-02-17T00:00Z, within its category window) and role, and each ID is used at most twice. Every number is a card value with its session tag or appears in a headline cited in the same part; no spot-FX levels or returns (DXY only); currency direction comes from dated reporting. Previews are never used for outcomes; pending events are referred to as the next print or update without dates. Process note: the scratchpad directory is shared with other writers, and one dump read early on (a poland_pl topic listing with 203 items) belonged to another date. Nothing from it was used; all work then moved to a date-named private folder, and the card and digest were re-run and confirmed identical to own-date output.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n1508 (AP, 'US official: Russia adds 7K more troops near Ukraine border'): the briefing was on the US evening of 16 February and may fall after 00:00 UTC; omitted, and the build-up is cited only through NATO statements made during the European day (n1498, n1502).
US January retail sales (16 February): no own-date headline reports the outcome, so no figure or direction is given.
Japan January trade (16 February 23:50 UTC): no own-date headline, so it is omitted; Japan uses the Q4 GDP rebound (n1548) instead.
Australia January labour force (17 February 00:30 UTC): after cutoff; only 'the next labour-force print' is mentioned.

Walmart, Palantir and Roku results and Intel's investor meeting (17 February): pending, with no dated preview headline; they appear only as Walmart's 'next print' and Intel's 'next strategy update', with no dates or outcomes.

After-hours reactions to Nvidia and Cisco (16 February): not reported in own-date headlines; only pre-results closes are quoted. DoorDash's 24% jump comes from n0847 and is labelled as following the regular-session close of 94.89 USD.

n0245 (Reuters, 'China's inflation slows, leaving room for policy easing'): stamped 15 February although China's January CPI was released at 01:30 UTC on 16 February; used for direction only, without naming a month or figure.
Live blogs rejected: n1308, n1297, n0331, n1256 (Reuters LIVE MARKETS).

Misdated or irrelevant items avoided: n1275 (Euronews, German manufacturing in 'October', stamped 11 February); n0651 and n0526 (2026 stock lists); n1176 (ESPN 2026); n1102 ('Super Bowl LVII'); n0487 (2021 APEC envoy); n0942 and n0491 (2034 market reports).

Spot-FX: n1653 (Bankier.pl) carries a numeric EUR/PLN level, and it is cited only for the zloty's direction (strongest in eight months); n1232 (TorFX Pound/Euro) and n1238 (Investing.com EUR/USD) are omitted; n0254 (yuan) and n0114 (dollar) are used for direction only.

Contradictory claims presented as attributed rather than resolved: Russia's claimed partial pull-back (n1475) against NATO's continuing build-up (n1498, n1502); Iran talks in 'very final stages' (n1506) against stalled talks (n1447, n1448).

Promotional or quote-page items not used: Stocktwits ticker pages (n1884, n1864), Yahoo Finance Singapore and TradingView quote pages, CryptoRank token-sale review (n0963), X2Y2 token launch (n1028), the Shopify corporate blog (n1178) and listicle-style stock picks.
Upstart's +35.65% session: no own-date headline gives the cause, so it is quoted only as a price move.
n1510 (Sky News, Lavrov threatening retaliation over UK sanctions): the underlying event date is unclear, so it is omitted.
n1866 and n1867 (Truth Social 'slated to launch next week', DWAC): left to the retail section; nonretail avoids the undated calendar wording.
n0016 (RBA February decision statement): cited only as the policy baseline; the title states no rate outcome, so none is claimed.
